question.text: Under SEBI's mutual fund disclosure framework, the scheme-specific rights of unit-holders (including the right to receive dividend, the right to inspect documents, and the right to exit at NAV without exit load when fundamental attributes of the scheme are changed) are detailed primarily in which document?

answer.text: Statement of Additional Information (SAI), which covers AMC-level and statutory information common to all schemes
Account Statement issued by the Registrar

explanation.text: The Logic: The SID is the scheme-specific offering document and contains the dedicated "Rights of Unit-holders" section that enumerates scheme-level rights such as the right to receive dividend, the right to inspect documents, and the right to exit at NAV without exit load when fundamental attributes of the scheme are changed. By tying the stem to scheme-specific rights, the SID is the uniquely correct location. The Trap: The SAI also references rights of unit-holders at the AMC/statutory level, which is why the audit flagged this item as ambiguous in its original wording. The revised stem narrows the scope to scheme-specific rights and fundamental-attribute exits, which sit in the SID. The KIM is only a summary of the SID and does not enumerate all rights. The Account Statement records only transactions and holdings. Note: The original stem ("rights of unit-holders are detailed in...") was ambiguous because the NISM Series V-A workbook says both SID and SAI discuss unit-holder rights (workbook pp.97 and 103). The stem has been tightened to scheme-specific rights and the exit-on-fundamental-change right, both of which the workbook lists under SID, making the keyed answer uniquely correct.
